context_pill: Capital Gains Computation for Inherited Property with Mortgage Clearance
example_summary: Abraham inherited a house from Xavier, paid off the remaining mortgage debt for a clear title, and later sold the property for ₹ 55 lacs. We examine the computation of capital gains for A.Y. 2026-27.
source_provision:
### Master Statutory Summary Matrix

| Statutory Provision | Core Condition / Applicability | Tax Treatment / Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 49(1)(iiia)** | Acquisition of capital asset under a gift, will, or succession | Cost to previous owner is adopted as the cost of acquisition for the new owner |
| **Section 48 & Section 55(2)** | Payment made by successor to clear outstanding mortgage debt for clear title | Expenditure incurred to remove encumbrance forms part of Cost of Acquisition |


- **(i)** Under Section 49(1)(iiia), when a capital asset is acquired by way of inheritance or under a will, the cost of acquisition to the assessee shall be the cost for which the previous owner acquired it.
- **(ii)** As settled by the Apex Court in RM. Arunachalam v. CIT, payments made by a successor to discharge a mortgage debt to obtain a clear title are treated as cost of acquisition.


> [!IMPORTANT] Judicial Precedent Rule: The Supreme Court ruling in RM. Arunachalam v. CIT establishes that mortgage redemption expenses incurred by a legal heir constitute an integral part of the cost of acquisition under Section 48.

director.justification: The problem requires calculating the final taxable capital gain by aggregating the cost to the previous owner and the mortgage redemption payment as per judicial precedent.
director.visual_metaphor: A property ledger where a 'Mortgage Debt' stamp is replaced by a 'Cost of Acquisition' entry to clear the title.

beat_plan.beat_goal: Establish the timeline of the property from Xavier's purchase to Abraham's sale and mortgage clearance.
Explain the cost of acquisition for inherited property under Section 49(1).
Apply the judicial precedent for mortgage redemption as a cost component.
Compute the final taxable capital gain by subtracting total costs from sale consideration.
State the final tax consequence for the relevant assessment year.
